# Ethan Yang

> Ethan Yang is a product engineer and product manager studying Information Science (minor in Computer Science) at Cornell University, class of 2028.

## Education

- Cornell University, B.A. Information Science, minor in Computer Science (2024–2028).
- Milstein Scholar: one of 25 selected for a four-year track in human-technology interaction research.
- Ran a 300-person hackathon with the Claude Builders Club. Member of Armada, a builder club.

## Experience

- SafetyWing (YC-backed insurtech), Product Engineering Intern, summer 2026. Shipped production code for an internal automation and compliance platform serving 30,000+ members. Built a harness that let AI coding agents migrate ~150 dashboard files, each tested in its own Docker container. Designed an automated payment reconciliation system that recovered ~$20k/month. Built and launched Autoview, which generates dashboard pages from the API spec and flags pages that break when the API changes.
- Cornell Tech, Milstein Summer Fellow, summer 2025. Owned product and built the filtering UI for IoNYC, an open-source React platform making 12,000+ NYC Participatory Budgeting ideas searchable. Led 15+ user interviews with NYC Council staff; piloted with the NYC Civic Engagement Commission.

## Projects

- HSPorter (hsporter.com), co-founder. AI tariff classification with human-in-the-loop review. Selected for an in-person Y Combinator interview. Built a RAG pipeline that cut LLM cost per query ~80% at 95% top-3 accuracy across 19,000+ tariff codes.
- Scout (getscout.me). An AI trip planner you add to your group text. 1st Place, Photon Track, BigRed//Hacks.
- Ithaca Insights (ithacainsights.com), lead developer. Open-source dashboard showing Ithaca renters whether a listing is overpriced. Vue + Leaflet frontend, FastAPI backend, natural-language map search without an LLM.

## Writing

- [Lessons from Watergate: What We Learned from the Media in Scandal](https://ethanyang.io/writings/watergate). The Concord Review, Volume 34, Number 3, Spring 2024, pp. 171–198. Argues that the press contributed little to the Watergate investigation itself: the FBI, the courts, whistleblowers and congressional committees uncovered it and ended Nixon's presidency, while the media carried their findings to the public and cast itself as a fourth actor in the separation of powers.

## The site

- Every planet and named moon, positioned for the current moment from astronomy-engine (VSOP87) and JPL mean orbital elements.
- Drawn at one pixel per pixel with no size floor: a body too small to cover a pixel is left undrawn, and its label marks the spot.
